newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn, soy harvest make slow advances.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn, soy harvest make slow advances.

text.p: Indiana corn and soybean harvests advanced slowly during the week ended Sunday and the condition of both crops was nearly unchanged from the previous week, said the state's Agricultural Statistics Service in its weekly report.
Scattered showers at mid-week slowed most field activities.

Corn was rated 44 percent good to excellent, unchanged from the previous week and compared with 34 a year ago. Five percent of the corn was harvested versus 20 a year ago and the average of 17. Fifty-three percent was mature versus 92 a year ago and the 79 average.

Soybeans were rated 40 percent good to excellent versus 39 a week ago. Three percent of the crop was harvested versus 26 a year ago and the 20 average. Twenty percent was mature versus 74 a year ago and the 70 average.
Eight percent of the winter wheat was seeded versus 11 for both a year ago and the average.
Pastures were rated two percent excellent, 30 good, 43 fair, 19 poor and six very poor.
Topsoil moisture was rated 19 percent surplus, 72 adequate seven short and two very short. Subsoil moisture was rated six percent surplus, 66 adequate and 24 short and four very short.
